frames.narration: A team creates a job: send the invoice email at 09:00. The API saves it in the jobs database with its next run time.

At 08:59:55 the scheduler that owns this job's range asks the database for jobs due in the next few seconds. It finds inv-7, marks it as queued with a conditional update, and puts it on the ready queue.
Worker A takes the job at 09:00. The queue does not delete it. It hides it for a 30-second lease and waits for an acknowledgement.
Worker A records the run, keyed by the job id and the scheduled time, and starts sending the email. Then the machine dies. No acknowledgement is ever sent.
Thirty seconds pass without an ack, so the lease runs out and the queue makes inv-7 visible again.
Worker B receives the job. It is the second attempt.

Worker B checks the run records. The earlier attempt started the run, and the email is sent with an idempotency key made from the job id, so it is sent once whether or not the first attempt got that far. B finishes the work.

B acknowledges the job and the queue deletes it. The scheduler computes the next run for a recurring job, or the job is finished. If B had failed too, the job would retry with growing delays and then go to the dead-letter queue.
